title: Governor of Colorado

context.text: Open seat: Democratic Gov. Jared Polis is ineligible to seek a third consecutive term.
In the June 30 Democratic primary, Attorney General Phil Weiser defeated U.S. Sen. Michael Bennet, 56.9% to 43.1%.
In the June 30 Republican primary, Victor Marx (39.9%) narrowly defeated state Sen. Barbara Kirkmeyer (39.4%) and state Rep. Scott Bottoms (20.8%).

The Colorado Secretary of State's certified general-election list shows seven gubernatorial tickets: Democratic, Republican, American Constitution, Libertarian, Unity, Approval Voting, and Greg Lopez (listed as Unaffiliated). Each candidate runs jointly with a lieutenant governor candidate.

candidates.name: Phil Weiser
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Lt. Gov. candidate Lesley Dahlkemper, a Jefferson County commissioner. Won the June 30 Democratic primary over U.S. Sen. Michael Bennet.

summary.text: Phil Weiser is Colorado's Attorney General, first elected in 2018 and re-elected in 2022, and the Democratic nominee for governor. Before that he was dean of the University of Colorado Law School and served in the Clinton and Obama administrations. His campaign platform emphasizes housing, health care, public safety and defending state laws against federal action.

background.text: Born in New York; B.A. from Swarthmore College (1990) and J.D. from New York University School of Law (1994).
Clerked for U.S. Supreme Court Justices Byron White and Ruth Bader Ginsburg; served as senior counsel in the Justice Department's Antitrust Division (1996–1998) and later in the Obama administration.
Dean of the University of Colorado Law School, 2011–2016; elected Colorado Attorney General in 2018 and re-elected in 2022.

priorities.text: Housing: increase attainable owner-occupied homes by 40,000, speed up permitting and expand down payment assistance.
Health care: a 'Healthy Colorado Plan' including 'Primary Care for All' and building on the Colorado Option.
Public safety: fund and recruit law enforcement, support gun safety laws and expand co-responder programs.

positions.summary: Campaign platform pledges to support recruitment and investment in police and sheriffs.
positions.quote: Support recruitment and investment in police and sheriffs— we need to fund law enforcement, expand and modernize law enforcement training, and support mental health resources for officers and all first responders.

positions.summary: Campaign platform pledges to sign, support and defend gun safety laws and strengthen the Office of Gun Violence Prevention.
positions.quote: Sign, support, and defend responsible gun safety laws —that will save lives and protect children.

positions.summary: Campaign platform pledges to defend reproductive rights, including Amendment 79.
positions.quote: Defend reproductive rights —including Amendment 79 and against any attacks on our laws protecting the right to choose.

positions.summary: Campaign platform pledges to enforce state laws that prevent the federal government from coercing state and local law enforcement into immigration enforcement.
positions.quote: Enforce state laws to prevent the federal government from coercing state and local law enforcement to conduct immigration enforcement activities and that bar sales of government facilities for ICE detention centers.

positions.summary: Campaign platform pledges to build on the Colorado Option to provide more affordable insurance coverage options and to ensure all those eligible for Medicaid are enrolled.

record.text: Co-led a coalition of 13 attorneys general in suing the U.S. Department of Energy and others over the termination of energy and infrastructure awards, including more than $600 million in Colorado projects.
Joined a coalition of 43 states and territories announcing a $400 million settlement in principle with Sandoz Inc. over alleged generic-drug price-fixing conspiracies.

Announced a settlement with Avail Property Management and PK Management over allegations that they denied prospective tenants housing by considering criminal-history information Colorado law prohibits landlords from using.

Announced a $2.86 million settlement with Staffing Network Holdings over allegations its former subsidiary overbilled the Colorado Department of Corrections for health care staffing, in violation of the Colorado False Claims Act.

candidates.name: Victor Marx
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Lt. Gov. candidate George Washington Markert, a retired Marine colonel. Won the June 30 Republican primary with 39.9% in a three-way race.

summary.text: Victor Marx is an author, minister and political newcomer who founded All Things Possible Ministries in 2003 and is the Republican nominee for governor. His platform calls for a phased reduction of the state income tax, expedited residential permitting, school choice, voter ID and required cooperation with federal immigration authorities.

background.text: Born in Lafayette, Louisiana; served in the U.S. Marine Corps, 1983–1986.
Founded All Things Possible Ministries in 2003; described as an author and minister.

The Colorado Sun described his life story as “extraordinary, albeit mostly unprovable,” including unverified claims of saving people, a fatal shooting and an air strike, and reported that it raises questions he has refused to answer; his campaign did not respond to a request for more detail about it.

priorities.text: Cutting taxes through a phased reduction of the state income tax when verified surpluses exist.
priorities.quote: As Governor, I will support a responsible and phased reduction of the state income tax rate under C.R.S. § 39-22-104 when verified revenue surpluses exist

priorities.text: Public safety, including grants, training and technology for local law enforcement.
Education choice and parental access to curriculum.

positions.summary: Would require state and local law enforcement to cooperate with federal immigration authorities, including ICE, when an arrestee is suspected of being unlawfully present and is charged with a crime.
positions.quote: I will require all state and local law enforcement agencies to cooperate with federal immigration authorities—including ICE and DHS—whenever an arrested individual is suspected of being unlawfully present and is charged with a crime.

positions.summary: Supports legislation letting parents choose among public, charter, magnet, online, homeschool or private options with funding following the student.
positions.quote: I will support legislation enabling parents to choose the best educational environment—public, charter, magnet, online, homeschool, or private—while ensuring that funding follows the student

candidates.researchNotes: Has not held public office, so no record items. Positions are drawn from the policies page of his campaign website; no direct statement was found there on guns, abortion or transgender athletes. His proposal to require voter ID was not mapped to the documentary-proof-of-citizenship issue because the page describes voter ID, not proof of citizenship. A 2026 Colorado Sun report discusses scrutiny of his personal backstory; the backstory item is worded to match the Colorado Sun text (“mostly unprovable”, “unverified claims”, questions he has “refused to answer”). Added Oct. 19: two statements shown without a stance (energy, from his policy page; housing, from a Summit Daily Q&A). His Q&A answer on taxing vacant homes concerns a state tax on property owners, not taxes on high earners, so it was not mapped to that issue. Colorado Public Radio's voter guide is behind a bot check and was not used.

statements.quote: As Governor, I will support an all-of-the-above energy strategy that expands renewable sources like wind, solar, and geothermal while maintaining the vital role of oil, gas, hydroelectric power, and emerging technologies such as modular nuclear and advanced storage systems.
Streamline permitting, cut regulatory red tape, end unfunded mandates on counties and give local communities, not Denver bureaucrats, the tools to create attainable housing that fits their needs.
statements.context: In a Summit Daily candidate Q&A, Oct. 7, 2026, on housing in the High Country

candidates.name: Greg Lopez
candidates.ballotNote: Running as an unaffiliated candidate with Lt. Gov. candidate Taralyn Romero, a property-rights advocate.

summary.text: Greg Lopez is a former U.S. representative from Colorado's 4th District (2024–2025) and a veteran, mayor and small-business owner, according to his campaign site. He is running as an independent after previously running as a Republican, and ran for governor in 2018 and 2022.

priorities.text: Government efficiency: zero-based budgeting and a Colorado version of the federal DOGE to review every agency and program.
priorities.quote: I will establish a Colorado version of DOGE focused on eliminating waste, duplication, unnecessary regulations, and inefficient spending.

priorities.text: Starter homes: building 25,000 modest starter homes in his first four years and reducing water and sewer tap costs.
priorities.quote: In my first four years, I will ensure that we build 25,000 starter homes.

priorities.text: Reforming the Colorado Department of Transportation, including seeking to purchase E-470 and remove its tolls.
priorities.quote: I will seek to purchase E470 and remove the tolls

positions.summary: Says Colorado gun laws of the past eight years infringe on constitutional rights and that he would oppose what he calls unconstitutional restrictions on responsible gun ownership.
positions.quote: For the last eight years, Colorado Legislature has been passing gun laws that are infringing on the constitutional rights of citizens and that needs to stop.

positions.summary: Says he would work to expand school choice, charter schools, home-schooling support and vocational training in every district.
positions.quote: As Governor, I will work towards expanding educational opportunities in every school district through school choice, charter schools, home schooling support, career pathways, and vocational training programs that prepare students for real-world success.

positions.summary: Says Colorado should fully cooperate with federal immigration enforcement involving violent criminals, drug traffickers, gang members and people who pose a threat to public safety; he also calls legal immigration important.
positions.quote: Colorado should fully cooperate with federal immigration enforcement efforts involving violent criminals, drug traffickers, gang members, and individuals who pose a threat to public safety.

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign issues page (greglopez.co/issues) lists 21 issues with first-person text. No page text found on rent regulation, minimum wage, tariffs, taxes on high earners, transgender athletes or public health coverage. His TABOR, qualified-immunity and parental-rights planks do not map to the listed issues.

statements.quote: I will continue to support policies that protect life while also supporting mothers, families, adoption services, healthcare access, and community-based support systems that help women and children thrive.
statements.context: On his campaign issues page, under “Promote and Respect Life”

statements.quote: Rising land costs, government fees, excessive regulations, permitting delays, and costly mandates have made it nearly impossible to build starter homes at prices working families can afford.
statements.context: On his campaign issues page; he also sets a goal of 25,000 starter homes in his first four years

statements.quote: I will lead Colorado in pursuing an “all-of-the-above” energy strategy that supports innovation, affordability, reliability, and job creation.
statements.context: On his campaign issues page, under “Energy Economy”

candidates.name: Stephen T. Hamilton
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Lt. Gov. candidate James K. Treibert.

summary.text: Stephen T. Hamilton is the American Constitution Party's nominee for governor, per the Colorado Secretary of State's certified candidate list.

priorities.text: Workforce housing: deed-restricted housing built by local housing authorities and employers, modular housing approvals and construction-defect and insurance reform.
Water: defending Colorado’s senior water rights and compact entitlements and fully funding the Colorado Water Plan.
priorities.quote: I will defend Colorado’s senior water rights and our compact entitlements

priorities.text: Budget reform: a top-to-bottom performance audit and a requirement that new programs identify their funding.
priorities.quote: I will order a top-to-bottom performance audit.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website found. Statements and priorities come from a Summit Daily Q&A and his own Summit Daily opinion column. His answers cover housing, water, wolves and the budget; no text found on abortion, guns, immigration, school choice or the other listed issues. Ballotpedia and Colorado Public Radio pages were not accessible.

statements.quote: As governor, I would push for High Country-specific tools: expand state incentives for deed-restricted, workforce housing built by local housing authorities and employers, accelerate modular and manufactured housing approvals, and unlock underused state and federal land near existing infrastructure.
statements.context: In a Summit Daily candidate Q&A, Oct. 7, 2026, on High Country housing

statements.quote: As governor, I will order a top-to-bottom performance audit, enforce PAYGO — any new program must identify its funding — and modernize Medicaid delivery to cut waste, not eligibility.
statements.context: In a Summit Daily candidate Q&A, Oct. 7, 2026, on the state budget

candidates.name: Eric Mulder
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Lt. Gov. candidate Wayne Harlos.

summary.text: Eric Mulder is the Libertarian Party's nominee for governor, per the Colorado Secretary of State's certified candidate list.

priorities.text: Keeping tax dollars local: a one-year exemption from the state sales tax for economically distressed communities, which could replace it with a local tax subject to voter approval.
Privacy: opposing government-operated Flock license-plate cameras.
priorities.quote: As governor, I will oppose the expansion of government-operated Flock cameras

priorities.text: Energy: a path for small modular nuclear reactors in Colorado.
priorities.quote: Work with the legislature to create a clean path for small modular reactors to become a large part of Colorado energy production

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign site rendered in headless Chromium; Priorities and On the Issues pages read. No page text found on abortion, guns, immigration, housing, minimum wage, tariffs or the other listed issues.

statements.quote: The first step is agreeing that government should not decide which energy source it prefers.
statements.context: On the Issues page of his campaign site, under Energy; the page also covers oil and gas, solar, wind, coal and nuclear

statements.quote: Reduce administrative burdens on Medicaid through directing the Department of Health Care Policy and Financing to review existing processes and requirements to determine if they are excessive and to eliminate duplicate paperwork
statements.context: On the Issues page of his campaign site, under Healthcare

candidates.name: Jeff Peckman
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Lt. Gov. candidate T.J. Cole. Won the Unity Party primary 146–126 over Paul Noel Fiorino.

summary.text: Jeff Peckman is the Unity Party's nominee for governor and is described as a UFO disclosure activist. He won his party's primary with 146 votes (53.7%).

priorities.text: Declaring a state of emergency on air pollution.
priorities.quote: I would declare a state of emergency on air pollution.

priorities.text: Creating a Partnership for Applied Coherence Technologies (P.A.C.T.) to launch new technologies.
priorities.quote: Create the Partnership for Applied Coherence Technologies (P.A.C.T.)

candidates.researchNotes: Sources are a Summit Daily Q&A, his Summit Daily opinion column and the Solutions Blueprint on his campaign site, which says he does not take a conventional “position” on listed issues and instead offers technology-based proposals. Colorado Public Radio's voter guide is behind a bot check and was not used.

statements.quote: I would support adding more modular housing, zoning changes, creative financing and taxation to increase inventory and affordability.
statements.context: In a Summit Daily candidate Q&A, Oct. 7, 2026, on High Country housing

statements.quote: Climate change and air pollution are wreaking havoc on Colorado.
statements.context: In a Summit Daily candidate Q&A, Oct. 7, 2026; he proposes a state-level emergency declaration on air pollution and a vehicle-emissions device he describes as his own proposal

candidates.name: Erik Underwood
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Lt. Gov. candidate Frank Atwood.

summary.text: Erik Underwood is the Approval Voting Party's nominee for governor. His campaign site lists a child care program, a plan for universal health care, and ending the Taxpayer's Bill of Rights (TABOR).

priorities.text: Universal health care for Coloradans.
priorities.quote: Healthcare is a Human Right, Not a Privilege

priorities.text: Ending the Taxpayer’s Bill of Rights (TABOR).
priorities.quote: I originated the plan in 2018 to eliminate TABOR.

priorities.text: A child care program funded by optional 25-cent donations at checkout.

positions.summary: Says he would provide all Coloradans with free health care or, at minimum, a maximum of $50 per year per family member, funded in part through payroll and income taxes and a multi-state insurance pool.
positions.quote: I will provide all Coloradans with free healthcare, or at minimum $50 maximum per year per family member (with installment plans for lower-income families).

positions.summary: His environmental plan includes accelerating the transition to renewables with union labor standards and a fund for displaced fossil fuel workers, and a 2,000-foot setback for new oil and gas operations.
positions.quote: Accelerate transition to renewables paired with union labor standards and a Just Transition fund for displaced fossil fuel workers in Weld, Garfield, Moffat, and Rio Blanco counties.

candidates.researchNotes: Read five of his roughly two dozen issue pages (health care, environment, child care, justice and human rights, TABOR); his AIPAC, affordable-homes and LGBTQ+ pages were read but contain no statement that maps to a listed issue (the AIPAC page addresses lobbying disclosure and a state divestment law, not U.S. aid; the LGBTQ+ page has no athletics statement). Other pages were not opened.

statements.quote: What if we created a state optional program asking Colorado consumers for a one-time donation of 25 cents after each purchase to go toward a childcare fund?
statements.context: On his child care plan page, which proposes an optional-donation fund with a $250,000 household income limit

statements.quote: I will sign a bill holding ICE agents accountable for any constitutional or human rights violations in Colorado.
statements.context: On his Justice & Human Rights page

researchNotes: Slate confirmed 2026-10-19 against the Colorado Secretary of State's official certified general-election candidate list (seven gubernatorial tickets). Ballotpedia blocked automated access, so Wikipedia is used only for party/basic bio and primary results. Running mates are in each ballotNote (Markert's description as a retired Marine colonel is from Colorado Sun reporting, 2026-07-31). Basic depth for the two major-party nominees; minimal for the five minor candidates.
